ns2:course.label: Light
ns2:course.description: (PHYCS 371) Wave kinematics; geometrical optics: basic concepts, ray-tracing and matrix formalism, Gaussian imaging by thick lenses, stops, and apertures, and intensity relations; interference; interference spectroscopy and coherence; diffraction: Fresnel-Kirchhoff formulation, Fraunhofer case, Fresnel case, and holography; polarized light. Lectures, laboratory, and problems 4 undergraduate hours. 3 or 4 graduate hours (3 hours without lab). Prerequisite: PHYS 102 (includes PHYS 101), or PHYS 214 (includes PHYS 211and PHYS 212); MATH 385 or equivalent; or consent of instructor.
